records.issue_text: [BUG] The remindersToCancel loop POSTs to SendGrid with reminder.referenceId as batch_id, but reminders with cancelled=true can have referenceId=null (they were marked cancelled before ever being scheduled), so the SendGrid request fails. The thrown error is caught by the outer try/catch after the first null referenceId, aborting the whole loop — all remaining cancelled reminders (including ones with valid referenceIds) are never cancelled at SendGrid and never deleted from the DB in that run, so already-cancelled bookings keep sending reminder emails.
records.rationale: The diff shows `cancelled` is only set in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` when `referenceId` is truthy; if `referenceId` is null/absent, the reminder is deleted instead and never marked cancelled. Specifically: `if (!referenceId) { await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } }); return; }` and only later `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(... data: { cancelled: true })`. Therefore, within the code added/changed in this diff, a record with `cancelled=true` should not have `referenceId=null`, contradicting the finding’s premise about null `batch_id` aborting the loop.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cancellation sweep in the email scheduling endpoint queries ALL cancelled workflowReminders regardless of method and cancels them via SendGrid's /v3/user/scheduled_sends, then hard-deletes them from the database. This bug also means reminder-cancellation logic now lives in an unrelated scheduling endpoint rather than in the reminder managers, a placement not traceable to any stated requirement.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The per-reminder SendGrid cancel and the DB delete are wrapped in one try/catch whose only recovery is console.log, and deletes are collected then awaited only if no iteration threw. One failing SendGrid call (rate limit, transient 5xx) leaves all prior successful cancels' DB rows un-deleted (the Promise.all is skipped by the catch), so they are re-cancelled on every subsequent run indefinitely; operators see only a console.log with no retry or alerting. This inverted-retry loop is new behavior in this diff with no requirement calling for best-effort, silent-failure cleanup.
